passages: CME Group (NASDAQ: $CME) plans to launch futures contracts for Bitcoin Cash (CRYPTO: $BCH) and Uniswap (CRYPTO: $UNI) on October 19, expanding its crypto derivatives lineup.
Bitcoin Cash futures will represent 250 BCH per contract, while Micro Bitcoin Cash futures will represent 25 BCH.
Uniswap futures will cover 10,000 UNI, with Micro contracts representing 1,000 UNI.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.

"As crypto markets continue to mature, participants require broader, regulated tools to navigate evolving digital asset related price risk," Giovanni Vicioso, CME Group's global head of cryptocurrency products, said in a statement.
The launch comes as institutional investors seek more ways to hedge exposure to cryptocurrencies beyond Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) and Ether (CRYPTO: $ETH), according to CME.

The new contracts will add to CME's existing futures offerings covering assets including Bitcoin, Ether, XRP (CRYPTO: $XRP), Solana (CRYPTO: $SOL), Cardano (CRYPTO: $ADA), Chainlink (CRYPTO: $LINK), Stellar (CRYPTO: $XLM), Avalanche (CRYPTO: $AVAX) and Sui (CRYPTO: $SUI).

The price action is the part retail traders will remember, and it's worth being honest about what it means and what it doesn't.
The launch itself is still three weeks out and explicitly contingent on regulatory review, the same review every CME crypto product has to clear before it goes live.

CME says Cardano, Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche and Sui futures already topped $1 billion in combined volume this year.
The Micro sizing matters more than it sounds.
That's CME building out what now looks like a full institutional menu of the crypto assets with the deepest liquidity and clearest regulatory standing.
But demand from clients is also, bluntly, demand CME can see in its own order flow and in the flow of the regulated derivatives desks it serves.
This isn't a popularity contest decided by social media sentiment.
It's an exchange following where hedging demand already exists.
The Metropolix, from Startup Fortune: your own building and public page on the map, plus a Startup Fortune feature with annual plans.
When it decides an asset is worth a futures contract, that's effectively Wall Street's own credential-check, and BCH holders and UNI holders just got theirs.

Bitcoin Cash traders didn't wait for the October 19 start date to move. CME Group said on September 22 that it plans to list Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap futures starting October 19, pending regulatory review. The news landed hard. Bitcoin Cash jumped from roughly $267 to the $300s within hours, a move Forbes pegged as high as 36% to $366, while CoinMarketCap and 24/7 Wall St. put the surge closer to 24% to 30%. The exact number depends on which exchange and which hour you check, but the direction is not in dispute: this was one of the sharpest reactions to a derivatives listing announcement crypto markets have seen all year. That alone tells you something about where institutional money thinks the next leg of crypto adoption is headed. CME isn't a speculative trading venue chasing retail flow. It's the exchange pension funds, hedge funds, and commodity trading desks use to hedge regulated risk. When it decides an asset is worth a futures contract, that's effectively Wall Street's own credential-check, and BCH holders and UNI holders just got theirs. The standard Bitcoin Cash future will represent 250 BCH, with a Micro BCH contract sized at 25 BCH, mirroring the structure CME already uses for its Bitcoin and Ether products. Uniswap gets the same two-tier treatment: a standard contract covering 10,000 UNI and a Micro contract covering 1,000 UNI. The Micro sizing matters more than it sounds. It's how CME lets smaller funds and even well-capitalized individual traders get regulated exposure without needing the balance sheet for a full-size contract, and it's the same playbook that made Micro Bitcoin and Micro Ether futures some of the exchange's fastest-growing products after their own launches. Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap will become the sixth and seventh single-asset altcoin futures CME has added this year alone, joining Solana, Cardano, Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche and Sui on top of the original Bitcoin, Ether and XRP contracts. That's not a cautious toe in the water. That's CME building out what now looks like a full institutional menu of the crypto assets with the deepest liquidity and clearest regulatory standing. Grayscale filed an amended S-3 to convert its Bitcoin Cash Trust into a spot ETF listed as BCHG on NYSE Arca, and BCH jumped as much as 12% on the news even though the SEC hasn't approved the listing rule it depends on. Grayscale has also filed similar conversion paperwork for its Hedera and Litecoin trusts as the SEC's faster generic listing... - grayscale bitcoin cash trust spot ETF listing - bitcoin cash price surge after SEC filing announcement And the volume backs up the ambition. According to CME Group's own release, the altcoin futures it rolled out earlier in 2026, Cardano, Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche and Sui, have already generated more than $1 billion in combined notional trading volume year to date. This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them. CME Group ( NASDAQ: CME | CME Price Prediction ), the Chicago-based derivatives exchange, is preparing to list futures contracts for Bitcoin Cash ( CRYPTO: BCH ) and Uniswap ( CRYPTO: UNI ) on October 19, 2026, pending regulatory approval. Bitcoin Cash, a payment-focused spin-off of Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ), is a separate network, while UNI serves as the governance token for Uniswap, a decentralized exchange that lets users trade tokens directly without intermediaries. As both cryptocurrencies approach their futures listing, they face challenges. Uniswap is priced around $7 after a 10.4% decline over the week, while Bitcoin Cash is trading at about $264, down 10.7% in the same timeframe. Typically, traders view the announcement of new futures as a potential buy signal. But do futures contracts tend to push a coin’s price up, down, or remain neutral? Futures contracts are agreements to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on a future date. On the CME, these contracts trade on a regulated exchange with a clearing house that ensures both parties fulfill their agreements, minimizing the risk of default. For Bitcoin Cash, each standard futures contract covers 250 BCH, while a micro contract covers 25 BCH. Similarly, the standard Uniswap contract represents 10,000 UNI, with a smaller micro version covering 1,000 UNI. This structure allows larger institutions to trade significant amounts while smaller traders can participate without committing to a full contract. The new listings join an existing suite of cryptocurrency futures that includes Bitcoin, Ether ( CRYPTO: ETH ), XRP ( CRYPTO: XRP ), Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ), Cardano ( CRYPTO: ADA ), Chainlink ( CRYPTO: LINK ), Stellar ( CRYPTO: XLM ), Avalanche ( CRYPTO: AVAX ), and Sui ( CRYPTO: SUI ). According to CME, expanding into Cardano , Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche, and Sui futures has added over $1 billion in total contract value this year. In the first half of 2026, CME’s crypto futures and options averaged 279,800 contracts traded daily, worth about $8.3 billion in total value. The average open interest—the total number of contracts still active—was 264,600 contracts, valued at $15.4 billion. However, historical data shows that launch days are often modest. For example, when Ether futures debuted on CME in February 2021, the first-day volume was only 388 contracts, representing roughly 19,400 ETH worth about $33 million, at an average of $1,700 per Ether. Compared with today’s daily trading volume, the initial figures for new contracts are quite small. Hedging is the practice of taking an opposite position to mitigate risk, such as a Bitcoin Cash holder going short on CME to protect against price drops rather than selling coins, which can take pressure off the spot market where coins are traded immediately. Conversely, short selling profits from a price decline. With futures, traders can take short positions without first borrowing the asset, giving sellers a new, regulated tool they didn’t previously have. The disparity between the futures price and the spot price, known as the basis, can impact trading decisions. If the futures price is higher than the spot price, a fund might buy the asset and sell the futures contract, profiting from the difference when both prices converge at expiry. passages: CME is adding Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap futures to its regulated exchange, but history shows these listings can push prices in opposite directions depending on who shows up to trade first.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

CME Group ( NASDAQ: CME | CME Price Prediction ), the Chicago-based derivatives exchange, is preparing to list futures contracts for Bitcoin Cash ( CRYPTO: BCH ) and Uniswap ( CRYPTO: UNI ) on October 19, 2026, pending regulatory approval. Bitcoin Cash, a payment-focused spin-off of Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ), is a separate network, while UNI serves as the governance token for Uniswap, a decentralized exchange that lets users trade tokens directly without intermediaries.

As both cryptocurrencies approach their futures listing, they face challenges. Uniswap is priced around $7 after a 10.4% decline over the week, while Bitcoin Cash is trading at about $264, down 10.7% in the same timeframe.
Typically, traders view the announcement of new futures as a potential buy signal. But do futures contracts tend to push a coin’s price up, down, or remain neutral?

Futures contracts are agreements to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on a future date. On the CME, these contracts trade on a regulated exchange with a clearing house that ensures both parties fulfill their agreements, minimizing the risk of default.

For Bitcoin Cash, each standard futures contract covers 250 BCH, while a micro contract covers 25 BCH. Similarly, the standard Uniswap contract represents 10,000 UNI, with a smaller micro version covering 1,000 UNI. This structure allows larger institutions to trade significant amounts while smaller traders can participate without committing to a full contract.

The new listings join an existing suite of cryptocurrency futures that includes Bitcoin, Ether ( CRYPTO: ETH ), XRP ( CRYPTO: XRP ), Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ), Cardano ( CRYPTO: ADA ), Chainlink ( CRYPTO: LINK ), Stellar ( CRYPTO: XLM ), Avalanche ( CRYPTO: AVAX ), and Sui ( CRYPTO: SUI ). According to CME, expanding into Cardano , Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche, and Sui futures has added over $1 billion in total contract value this year.

In the first half of 2026, CME’s crypto futures and options averaged 279,800 contracts traded daily, worth about $8.3 billion in total value. The average open interest—the total number of contracts still active—was 264,600 contracts, valued at $15.4 billion.

However, historical data shows that launch days are often modest. For example, when Ether futures debuted on CME in February 2021, the first-day volume was only 388 contracts, representing roughly 19,400 ETH worth about $33 million, at an average of $1,700 per Ether. Compared with today’s daily trading volume, the initial figures for new contracts are quite small.

Hedging is the practice of taking an opposite position to mitigate risk, such as a Bitcoin Cash holder going short on CME to protect against price drops rather than selling coins, which can take pressure off the spot market where coins are traded immediately.

Conversely, short selling profits from a price decline. With futures, traders can take short positions without first borrowing the asset, giving sellers a new, regulated tool they didn’t previously have.

The disparity between the futures price and the spot price, known as the basis, can impact trading decisions. If the futures price is higher than the spot price, a fund might buy the asset and sell the futures contract, profiting from the difference when both prices converge at expiry. This process simultaneously buys the asset and sells the futures contract, allowing traders to benefit regardless of the price direction.

Moreover, certain institutional investors, such as pension funds , may not be allowed to hold cryptocurrencies directly but can participate in trading listed futures. This broader access may bring in more buyers, while short selling could increase selling pressure, creating a complex dynamic around price movement.

CME promotes the futures contracts as tools for risk management. Giovanni Vicioso, CME Group’s global head of cryptocurrency products, said, “As crypto markets continue to mature, participants require broader, regulated tools to navigate evolving digital asset-related price risk.”

Both Uniswap and Bitcoin Cash are entering this futures market after experiencing a rough week. Investors hoping for the new listing to reverse the downward trend should remember that while it could attract new buyers, it also welcomes short sellers who might increase selling pressure.

The overall impact will depend on which type of trader dominates the market. If hedgers and newly eligible institutional investors lead, futures may reduce selling pressure. Conversely, if short sellers dominate trading, it could add to downward pressure.
Early trading volume will also play a crucial role; if the contracts see limited activity, as with Ether’s launch, they could have minimal impact compared to regular spot trading of these coins.
In summary, while CME futures may add volatility, predicting a definitive price move for Uniswap and Bitcoin Cash remains uncertain, as the listing brings both buying and selling pressure into play.

The first check is whether both contracts go live on October 19 or slip due to regulatory review. After that, CME’s daily open interest reports are the figure to follow. If open interest rises week after week through November while both coins rally, hedgers and new institutions are outweighing short sellers. If open interest grows while both prices fall, the short side is winning.

The exact number depends on which exchange and which hour you check, but the direction is not in dispute: this was one of the sharpest reactions to a derivatives listing announcement crypto markets have seen all year. That alone tells you something about where institutional money thinks the next leg of crypto adoption is headed. CME isn't a speculative trading venue chasing retail flow. The standard Bitcoin Cash future will represent 250 BCH, with a Micro BCH contract sized at 25 BCH, mirroring the structure CME already uses for its Bitcoin and Ether products. Uniswap gets the same two-tier treatment: a standard contract covering 10,000 UNI and a Micro contract covering 1,000 UNI. The Micro sizing matters more than it sounds. It's how CME lets smaller funds and even well-capitalized individual traders get regulated exposure without needing the balance sheet for a full-size contract, and it's the same playbook that made Micro Bitcoin and Micro Ether futures some of the exchange's fastest-growing products after their own launches. Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap will become the sixth and seventh single-asset altcoin futures CME has added this year alone, joining Solana, Cardano, Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche and Sui on top of the original Bitcoin, Ether and XRP contracts. That's not a cautious toe in the water. That's CME building out what now looks like a full institutional menu of the crypto assets with the deepest liquidity and clearest regulatory standing. Grayscale filed an amended S-3 to convert its Bitcoin Cash Trust into a spot ETF listed as BCHG on NYSE Arca, and BCH jumped as much as 12% on the news even though the SEC hasn't approved the listing rule it depends on. Grayscale has also filed similar conversion paperwork for its Hedera and Litecoin trusts as the SEC's faster generic listing... - grayscale bitcoin cash trust spot ETF listing - bitcoin cash price surge after SEC filing announcement And the volume backs up the ambition. According to CME Group's own release, the altcoin futures it rolled out earlier in 2026, Cardano, Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche and Sui, have already generated more than $1 billion in combined notional trading volume year to date. Across its whole crypto suite, CME reported first-half 2026 average daily volume of 279,800 contracts worth $8.3 billion in notional value, with average open interest of 264,600 contracts worth $15.4 billion, figures confirmed in reporting from Crypto Economy and The Block. Those aren't rounding errors. That's a real, sustained institutional book. Why Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap specifically, and not some other token sitting in the top twenty? CME said the expansion responds to client demand for institutional-grade risk management tools in high-liquidity altcoin markets, and both assets fit that description on paper: Bitcoin Cash has traded on major venues since its 2017 fork from Bitcoin, and Uniswap's UNI token sits on top of the largest decentralized exchange by volume in DeFi. But demand from clients is also, bluntly, demand CME can see in its own order flow and in the flow of the regulated derivatives desks it serves. This isn't a popularity contest decided by social media sentiment. It's an exchange following where hedging demand already exists. The price action is the part retail traders will remember, and it's worth being honest about what it means and what it doesn't. A CME futures listing announcement is not the same as a futures listing. The launch itself is still three weeks out and explicitly contingent on regulatory review, the same review every CME crypto product has to clear before it goes live. Short squeezes and anticipatory buying, which Invezz reported played a role alongside renewed talk of a potential Grayscale Bitcoin Cash Trust conversion to an ETF, can evaporate just as fast once the news is priced in. Traders who bought the announcement are now betting that institutional futures volume actually materializes on October 19 and keeps building from there, not that the headline alone sustains a 30% repricing. What won't evaporate is the signal underneath the spike. Wall Street's biggest derivatives exchange just told the market, in writing, which two tokens it considers safe enough to put a regulated contract on. For an industry that spent years arguing about which altcoins were securities, commodities, or something in between, that's a far more concrete answer than any regulator has given so far. Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap will become the sixth and seventh single-asset altcoin futures CME has added this year alone, joining Solana, Cardano, Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche and Sui on top of the original Bitcoin, Ether and XRP contracts. That's not a cautious toe in the water. That's CME building out what now looks like a full institutional menu of the crypto assets with the deepest liquidity and clearest regulatory standing.

Grayscale filed an amended S-3 to convert its Bitcoin Cash Trust into a spot ETF listed as BCHG on NYSE Arca, and BCH jumped as much as 12% on the news even though the SEC hasn't approved the listing rule it depends on. Grayscale has also filed similar conversion paperwork for its Hedera and Litecoin trusts as the SEC's faster generic listing... - grayscale bitcoin cash trust spot ETF listing - bitcoin cash price surge after SEC filing announcement

And the volume backs up the ambition. According to CME Group's own release, the altcoin futures it rolled out earlier in 2026, Cardano, Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche and Sui, have already generated more than $1 billion in combined notional trading volume year to date. Across its whole crypto suite, CME reported first-half 2026 average daily volume of 279,800 contracts worth $8.3 billion in notional value, with average open interest of 264,600 contracts worth $15.4 billion, figures confirmed in reporting from Crypto Economy and The Block. Those aren't rounding errors. That's a real, sustained institutional book.

Why Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap specifically, and not some other token sitting in the top twenty? CME said the expansion responds to client demand for institutional-grade risk management tools in high-liquidity altcoin markets, and both assets fit that description on paper: Bitcoin Cash has traded on major venues since its 2017 fork from Bitcoin, and Uniswap's UNI token sits on top of the largest decentralized exchange by volume in DeFi. But demand from clients is also, bluntly, demand CME can see in its own order flow and in the flow of the regulated derivatives desks it serves. This isn't a popularity contest decided by social media sentiment. It's an exchange following where hedging demand already exists.

The price action is the part retail traders will remember, and it's worth being honest about what it means and what it doesn't. A CME futures listing announcement is not the same as a futures listing. The launch itself is still three weeks out and explicitly contingent on regulatory review, the same review every CME crypto product has to clear before it goes live. Short squeezes and anticipatory buying, which Invezz reported played a role alongside renewed talk of a potential Grayscale Bitcoin Cash Trust conversion to an ETF, can evaporate just as fast once the news is priced in. Traders who bought the announcement are now betting that institutional futures volume actually materializes on October 19 and keeps building from there, not that the headline alone sustains a 30% repricing.

What won't evaporate is the signal underneath the spike. Wall Street's biggest derivatives exchange just told the market, in writing, which two tokens it considers safe enough to put a regulated contract on. For an industry that spent years arguing about which altcoins were securities, commodities, or something in between, that's a far more concrete answer than any regulator has given so far.

CME Group ( NASDAQ: CME | CME Price Prediction ), the Chicago-based derivatives exchange, is preparing to list futures contracts for Bitcoin Cash ( CRYPTO: BCH ) and Uniswap ( CRYPTO: UNI ) on October 19, 2026, pending regulatory approval. Bitcoin Cash, a payment-focused spin-off of Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ), is a separate network, while UNI serves as the governance token for Uniswap, a decentralized exchange that lets users trade tokens directly without intermediaries. As both cryptocurrencies approach their futures listing, they face challenges. Uniswap is priced around $7 after a 10.4% decline over the week, while Bitcoin Cash is trading at about $264, down 10.7% in the same timeframe. Typically, traders view the announcement of new futures as a potential buy signal. But do futures contracts tend to push a coin’s price up, down, or remain neutral? Futures contracts are agreements to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on a future date. On the CME, these contracts trade on a regulated exchange with a clearing house that ensures both parties fulfill their agreements, minimizing the risk of default. For Bitcoin Cash, each standard futures contract covers 250 BCH, while a micro contract covers 25 BCH. Similarly, the standard Uniswap contract represents 10,000 UNI, with a smaller micro version covering 1,000 UNI. This structure allows larger institutions to trade significant amounts while smaller traders can participate without committing to a full contract. The new listings join an existing suite of cryptocurrency futures that includes Bitcoin, Ether ( CRYPTO: ETH ), XRP ( CRYPTO: XRP ), Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ), Cardano ( CRYPTO: ADA ), Chainlink ( CRYPTO: LINK ), Stellar ( CRYPTO: XLM ), Avalanche ( CRYPTO: AVAX ), and Sui ( CRYPTO: SUI ). According to CME, expanding into Cardano , Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche, and Sui futures has added over $1 billion in total contract value this year. In the first half of 2026, CME’s crypto futures and options averaged 279,800 contracts traded daily, worth about $8.3 billion in total value. The average open interest—the total number of contracts still active—was 264,600 contracts, valued at $15.4 billion. However, historical data shows that launch days are often modest. For example, when Ether futures debuted on CME in February 2021, the first-day volume was only 388 contracts, representing roughly 19,400 ETH worth about $33 million, at an average of $1,700 per Ether. Compared with today’s daily trading volume, the initial figures for new contracts are quite small. Hedging is the practice of taking an opposite position to mitigate risk, such as a Bitcoin Cash holder going short on CME to protect against price drops rather than selling coins, which can take pressure off the spot market where coins are traded immediately. Conversely, short selling profits from a price decline. With futures, traders can take short positions without first borrowing the asset, giving sellers a new, regulated tool they didn’t previously have. The disparity between the futures price and the spot price, known as the basis, can impact trading decisions. If the futures price is higher than the spot price, a fund might buy the asset and sell the futures contract, profiting from the difference when both prices converge at expiry. This process simultaneously buys the asset and sells the futures contract, allowing traders to benefit regardless of the price direction. Moreover, certain institutional investors, such as pension funds , may not be allowed to hold cryptocurrencies directly but can participate in trading listed futures. This broader access may bring in more buyers, while short selling could increase selling pressure, creating a complex dynamic around price movement. CME promotes the futures contracts as tools for risk management. Giovanni Vicioso, CME Group’s global head of cryptocurrency products, said, “As crypto markets continue to mature, participants require broader, regulated tools to navigate evolving digital asset-related price risk.” Both Uniswap and Bitcoin Cash are entering this futures market after experiencing a rough week. Investors hoping for the new listing to reverse the downward trend should remember that while it could attract new buyers, it also welcomes short sellers who might increase selling pressure. The overall impact will depend on which type of trader dominates the market. If hedgers and newly eligible institutional investors lead, futures may reduce selling pressure. Conversely, if short sellers dominate trading, it could add to downward pressure. Early trading volume will also play a crucial role; if the contracts see limited activity, as with Ether’s launch, they could have minimal impact compared to regular spot trading of these coins. In summary, while CME futures may add volatility, predicting a definitive price move for Uniswap and Bitcoin Cash remains uncertain, as the listing brings both buying and selling pressure into play. The first check is whether both contracts go live on October 19 or slip due to regulatory review. After that, CME’s daily open interest reports are the figure to follow. If open interest rises week after week through November while both coins rally, hedgers and new institutions are outweighing short sellers. Bitcoin Cash, a payment-focused spin-off of Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ), is a separate network, while UNI serves as the governance token for Uniswap, a decentralized exchange that lets users trade tokens directly without intermediaries.

As both cryptocurrencies approach their futures listing, they face challenges. Uniswap is priced around $7 after a 10.4% decline over the week, while Bitcoin Cash is trading at about $264, down 10.7% in the same timeframe.
Typically, traders view the announcement of new futures as a potential buy signal. But do futures contracts tend to push a coin’s price up, down, or remain neutral?

Futures contracts are agreements to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on a future date. On the CME, these contracts trade on a regulated exchange with a clearing house that ensures both parties fulfill their agreements, minimizing the risk of default.

For Bitcoin Cash, each standard futures contract covers 250 BCH, while a micro contract covers 25 BCH. Similarly, the standard Uniswap contract represents 10,000 UNI, with a smaller micro version covering 1,000 UNI. This structure allows larger institutions to trade significant amounts while smaller traders can participate without committing to a full contract.

The new listings join an existing suite of cryptocurrency futures that includes Bitcoin, Ether ( CRYPTO: ETH ), XRP ( CRYPTO: XRP ), Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ), Cardano ( CRYPTO: ADA ), Chainlink ( CRYPTO: LINK ), Stellar ( CRYPTO: XLM ), Avalanche ( CRYPTO: AVAX ), and Sui ( CRYPTO: SUI ). According to CME, expanding into Cardano , Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche, and Sui futures has added over $1 billion in total contract value this year.

In the first half of 2026, CME’s crypto futures and options averaged 279,800 contracts traded daily, worth about $8.3 billion in total value. The average open interest—the total number of contracts still active—was 264,600 contracts, valued at $15.4 billion.

However, historical data shows that launch days are often modest. For example, when Ether futures debuted on CME in February 2021, the first-day volume was only 388 contracts, representing roughly 19,400 ETH worth about $33 million, at an average of $1,700 per Ether. Compared with today’s daily trading volume, the initial figures for new contracts are quite small.

Hedging is the practice of taking an opposite position to mitigate risk, such as a Bitcoin Cash holder going short on CME to protect against price drops rather than selling coins, which can take pressure off the spot market where coins are traded immediately.

Conversely, short selling profits from a price decline. With futures, traders can take short positions without first borrowing the asset, giving sellers a new, regulated tool they didn’t previously have.

The disparity between the futures price and the spot price, known as the basis, can impact trading decisions. If the futures price is higher than the spot price, a fund might buy the asset and sell the futures contract, profiting from the difference when both prices converge at expiry. This process simultaneously buys the asset and sells the futures contract, allowing traders to benefit regardless of the price direction.

Moreover, certain institutional investors, such as pension funds , may not be allowed to hold cryptocurrencies directly but can participate in trading listed futures. This broader access may bring in more buyers, while short selling could increase selling pressure, creating a complex dynamic around price movement.

CME promotes the futures contracts as tools for risk management. Giovanni Vicioso, CME Group’s global head of cryptocurrency products, said, “As crypto markets continue to mature, participants require broader, regulated tools to navigate evolving digital asset-related price risk.”

Both Uniswap and Bitcoin Cash are entering this futures market after experiencing a rough week. Investors hoping for the new listing to reverse the downward trend should remember that while it could attract new buyers, it also welcomes short sellers who might increase selling pressure.

The overall impact will depend on which type of trader dominates the market. If hedgers and newly eligible institutional investors lead, futures may reduce selling pressure. Conversely, if short sellers dominate trading, it could add to downward pressure.
Early trading volume will also play a crucial role; if the contracts see limited activity, as with Ether’s launch, they could have minimal impact compared to regular spot trading of these coins.
In summary, while CME futures may add volatility, predicting a definitive price move for Uniswap and Bitcoin Cash remains uncertain, as the listing brings both buying and selling pressure into play.

The first check is whether both contracts go live on October 19 or slip due to regulatory review. After that, CME’s daily open interest reports are the figure to follow. If open interest rises week after week through November while both coins rally, hedgers and new institutions are outweighing short sellers. If open interest grows while both prices fall, the short side is winning.

sources.title: The Tech Download: Amazon’s devices chief Panos Panay on tech giant's AI gadget push - CNBC
passages: Driving the current gadget and AI push is Amazon's hardware and services chief, Panos Panay, who's the latest guest on The Tech Download.
Amazon's foray into devices has seen it jump into speakers, doorbells and now wearables with its acquisition of Bee, a startup developing a wristband device.
Alexa is at the heart of tying all of those together in a world where "we might be moving away from a world of apps and screens," Panay said.
The smartphone has been at the center of our digital life for so long.
Now with more advanced AI, what if a screen isn't needed and instead you could do more with voice?
This is what Amazon, along with other device companies are thinking about.
What the best future gadgets look like is still up for debate.
But Amazon is certainly cooking a few things up.
My final big takeaway from the conversation was about semiconductors.
For those of you who know me, you know chips are one of my favorite topics.
For the first time publicly, Panay discussed Amazon's semiconductor efforts for its consumer electronics.
I remember using one and thinking there was definitely a future here for these kinds of devices.
Trump bought Apple, Nvidia and other tech giants before tariff reversal fueled rebound, according to a CNBC analysis.
This means that Amazon is designing the chips that go into its devices.
By having more control over the hardware and software integration, Amazon will be able to deliver more differentiated experiences around Alexa.
More than a decade ago, before we were talking about "AI agents," Amazon launched its digital voice assistant Alexa and the smart speaker branded Echo.
"I have a lab full of devices," Panay said, adding that there is a "whole roadmap of on-the-go devices."
"On some of the more critical devices right now, our focus is end-to-end silicon," Panay said.

sources.title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay sees a future where AI devices replace the need to use apps
passages: Alongside the launch of the company’s new AI wearables from Bee , Panos Panay, who serves as Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Alexa & Leo, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday to talk more in depth about where he sees personal computing headed.
With Bee — and ambient computing more generally — Panay also envisioned a future where the idea of interacting with apps becomes less important, as more tasks are handled via AI.
These gadgets passively record audio and take notes about your day, finding the to-dos, reminders, and insights you may later need to refer back to.
To balance the need to be useful with user privacy, Bee’s devices don’t actually store the raw audio from your conversations; they process the audio in real time and then delete it when done.
Transcripts of conversations are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls.
That means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you intentionally share them.
Rather, he believes a new crop of devices will emerge that use sensors to understand users better, and to bring intelligence to the world around you.
Amazon is placing its bets on ambient computing, not apps, as the future of personal AI.

“A lot of times, what you’re doing right now — what we all do right now — is we have to remember what we’re asking our tool to do for us,” Panay began, explaining that this is how we engage with our modern smartphones. “It’s like point, shoot, return,” Panay continued. “I think where we’re headed is a world [that] starts with ambient devices.”
Panay said that privacy was a key consideration for how these new ambient devices should work.

These gadgets passively record audio and take notes about your day, finding the to-dos, reminders, and insights you may later need to refer back to.
To balance the need to be useful with user privacy, Bee’s devices don’t actually store the raw audio from your conversations; they process the audio in real time and then delete it when done.
Transcripts of conversations are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls.
That means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you intentionally share them.
Rather, he believes a new crop of devices will emerge that use sensors to understand users better, and to bring intelligence to the world around you.

Panay said that privacy was a key consideration for how these new ambient devices should work.

Panos Panay, Amazon’s senior vice president of Devices, Alexa & Leo, said AI-enabled products could handle more tasks without apps, though he expects smartphones to remain important to personal computing. Speaking Thursday, Panay described ambient devices that use sensors and AI in the background to help identify what needs to be done. Instead of remembering which tool to ask or opening an app for each task, users could get help from devices that recognize a need and surface useful information. He said the approach could let people stay present and spend less time directing their tools. Panay sees a future in which people may ask technology to understand what they need instead of requesting a particular app. “I think there’s an intelligence layer that connects it all … and it has to be useful,” he said. He described that layer as a way to connect different devices, rather than a shift to one product type. Amazon’s two Bee devices offer examples of this approach. One is a band that can be worn on the wrist or detached and used as a pendant. The other is a credit-card-size accessory that attaches magnetically to a smartphone. The devices capture conversations to create notes and surface possible to-dos, reminders and insights for later use. Bee does not store raw audio. It processes audio in real time and deletes it when processing is finished. Conversation transcripts are encrypted with keys created and controlled by the user’s device. Others, including Amazon employees, cannot access the files unless the user chooses to share them. Panay said he does not expect one device form to replace another. Smartphones will remain part of personal computing, he said, as sensors and AI connect devices and bring assistance into more settings. His comments describe a possible direction for personal technology, rather than an immediate end to apps or phones. Simon Yoon reports on blockchain technology for TokenPost. coreStoryFacts.text: Driving the current gadget and AI push is Amazon's hardware and services chief, Panos Panay, who's the latest guest on The Tech Download.
Amazon's foray into devices has seen it jump into speakers, doorbells and now wearables with its acquisition of Bee, a startup developing a wristband device.
Alexa is at the heart of tying all of those together in a world where "we might be moving away from a world of apps and screens," Panay said.
The smartphone has been at the center of our digital life for so long.
Now with more advanced AI, what if a screen isn't needed and instead you could do more with voice?
This is what Amazon, along with other device companies are thinking about.
What the best future gadgets look like is still up for debate.
But Amazon is certainly cooking a few things up.
My final big takeaway from the conversation was about semiconductors.
For those of you who know me, you know chips are one of my favorite topics.
For the first time publicly, Panay discussed Amazon's semiconductor efforts for its consumer electronics.
I remember using one and thinking there was definitely a future here for these kinds of devices.
Trump bought Apple, Nvidia and other tech giants before tariff reversal fueled rebound, according to a CNBC analysis.
This means that Amazon is designing the chips that go into its devices.
By having more control over the hardware and software integration, Amazon will be able to deliver more differentiated experiences around Alexa.
More than a decade ago, before we were talking about "AI agents," Amazon launched its digital voice assistant Alexa and the smart speaker branded Echo.
"I have a lab full of devices," Panay said, adding that there is a "whole roadmap of on-the-go devices."
"On some of the more critical devices right now, our focus is end-to-end silicon," Panay said.

story.title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay sees a future where AI devices replace the need to use apps

facts.text: Driving the current gadget and AI push is Amazon's hardware and services chief, Panos Panay, who's the latest guest on The Tech Download.
Amazon's foray into devices has seen it jump into speakers, doorbells and now wearables with its acquisition of Bee, a startup developing a wristband device.
Alexa is at the heart of tying all of those together in a world where "we might be moving away from a world of apps and screens," Panay said.
The smartphone has been at the center of our digital life for so long.
Now with more advanced AI, what if a screen isn't needed and instead you could do more with voice?
This is what Amazon, along with other device companies are thinking about.
What the best future gadgets look like is still up for debate.
But Amazon is certainly cooking a few things up.
My final big takeaway from the conversation was about semiconductors.
For those of you who know me, you know chips are one of my favorite topics.
For the first time publicly, Panay discussed Amazon's semiconductor efforts for its consumer electronics.
I remember using one and thinking there was definitely a future here for these kinds of devices.
Trump bought Apple, Nvidia and other tech giants before tariff reversal fueled rebound, according to a CNBC analysis.
This means that Amazon is designing the chips that go into its devices.
By having more control over the hardware and software integration, Amazon will be able to deliver more differentiated experiences around Alexa.
More than a decade ago, before we were talking about "AI agents," Amazon launched its digital voice assistant Alexa and the smart speaker branded Echo.
"I have a lab full of devices," Panay said, adding that there is a "whole roadmap of on-the-go devices."
"On some of the more critical devices right now, our focus is end-to-end silicon," Panay said.

Alongside the launch of the company’s new AI wearables from Bee , Panos Panay, who serves as Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Alexa & Leo, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday to talk more in depth about where he sees personal computing headed.
With Bee — and ambient computing more generally — Panay also envisioned a future where the idea of interacting with apps becomes less important, as more tasks are handled via AI.
These gadgets passively record audio and take notes about your day, finding the to-dos, reminders, and insights you may later need to refer back to.
To balance the need to be useful with user privacy, Bee’s devices don’t actually store the raw audio from your conversations; they process the audio in real time and then delete it when done.
Transcripts of conversations are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls.
That means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you intentionally share them.
Rather, he believes a new crop of devices will emerge that use sensors to understand users better, and to bring intelligence to the world around you.
Amazon is placing its bets on ambient computing, not apps, as the future of personal AI.

“A lot of times, what you’re doing right now — what we all do right now — is we have to remember what we’re asking our tool to do for us,” Panay began, explaining that this is how we engage with our modern smartphones. “It’s like point, shoot, return,” Panay continued. “I think where we’re headed is a world [that] starts with ambient devices.”
Panay said that privacy was a key consideration for how these new ambient devices should work.

This is the app-less future Amazon is betting on.Speaking at the TechCrunch Disrupt event on Thursday, Panos Panay, Amazon’s Senior Vice President of Devices, Alexa & Leo, said the tech industry is moving toward a world of "ambient computing".

According to Panay, this ambient technology will allow people to put down their screens, stay more present with their friends and family, and stop worrying about missing important details.Meet Amazon's New "Bee" WearablesTo kickstart this new era, Amazon has launched a fresh lineup of AI gadgets under the "Bee" brand.

Panay, who spent 19 years at Microsoft's Surface computer division before joining Amazon, wants our gadgets to fade into the background.By using advanced sensors and AI, future devices will simply listen and figure out your tasks automatically.

Panay believes the next generation of users won't hunt for specific apps; they will simply expect their technology to understand their surroundings and get the job done.- EndsAlso Read | Amazon cuts nearly 1,000 jobs, retail employees in India impactedAlso Read | Amazon launches AI wearables that can listen in on your conversations and remember everythingAlso Read | Google says AI can help Indian farmers deal with climate change better

For instance, if you make dinner plans while talking to a friend, the AI can automatically draft a calendar invite.While users get 14 days of memory and basic summaries for free, an $11.99 monthly "Bee Pro" subscription unlocks unlimited memory and connects the AI directly to apps like Gmail, Outlook, and Amazon shopping.The Privacy QuestionA device that constantly listens to your day naturally raises major privacy concerns.
Amazon has tackled this by ensuring Bee devices do not store any raw audio recordings.

Furthermore, the text transcripts are locked using encryption keys that only your specific device controls, meaning not even Amazon employees can read your data.Even with these safety features in place, privacy experts still have concerns.
Panay described our current habit as "point, shoot, return", you have to remember exactly what you need and which app can do it.
Panay clarified that smartphones will remain important, noting that one piece of hardware rarely replaces another completely.Instead, a new "intelligence layer" will connect all our devices together.

Panos Panay, Amazon’s senior vice president of Devices, Alexa & Leo, said AI-enabled products could handle more tasks without apps, though he expects smartphones to remain important to personal computing.
Panos Panay described ambient devices that work in the background.
Panay said he does not expect one device form to replace another.
Amazon’s two Bee devices offer examples of this approach.

Panos Panay, Amazon’s senior vice president of Devices, Alexa & Leo, said AI-enabled products could handle more tasks without apps, though he expects smartphones to remain important to personal computing. Speaking Thursday, Panay described ambient devices that use sensors and AI in the background to help identify what needs to be done. Instead of remembering which tool to ask or opening an app for each task, users could get help from devices that recognize a need and surface useful information. He said the approach could let people stay present and spend less time directing their tools. Panay sees a future in which people may ask technology to understand what they need instead of requesting a particular app. “I think there’s an intelligence layer that connects it all … and it has to be useful,” he said. He described that layer as a way to connect different devices, rather than a shift to one product type. Amazon’s two Bee devices offer examples of this approach. One is a band that can be worn on the wrist or detached and used as a pendant. The other is a credit-card-size accessory that attaches magnetically to a smartphone. The devices capture conversations to create notes and surface possible to-dos, reminders and insights for later use. Bee does not store raw audio. It processes audio in real time and deletes it when processing is finished. Conversation transcripts are encrypted with keys created and controlled by the user’s device. Others, including Amazon employees, cannot access the files unless the user chooses to share them. Panay said he does not expect one device form to replace another. Smartphones will remain part of personal computing, he said, as sensors and AI connect devices and bring assistance into more settings. His comments describe a possible direction for personal technology, rather than an immediate end to apps or phones. Simon Yoon reports on blockchain technology for TokenPost. Muse Spark Open “is the most capable US open-weight model to date,” Meta’s chief of AI Alexandr Wang wrote on X. Unlike so-called closed models – such as Anthropic’s Claude or OpenAI’s ChatGPT – developers can download the parameters, known as weights and biases, of an open-weight model and modify them. Chinese developers have emerged as dominant players in the open-weight market for AI models over the past couple of years. Alibaba’s Qwen, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 and Z.ai’s GLM models have been considered open-weight frontrunners globally, but Meta claims its new open model now competes on a similar level. “Built for coding and agentic work,” Muse Spark Open “excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning,” Meta said in a blogpost, adding that “strong safeguards” have been integrated into the new model. Muse Spark Open is also “optimized” to run on Apple’s advanced M5 Ultra chips, Meta said, signaling an unusual partnership between the two tech companies. Muse Spark Open requires significant computing power. Users can run the model on two Mac Studios with M5 Ultra chips to create a “supercomputer” on their own desktop, Meta said. The launch comes just days after Meta announced its newest closed model, which it said rivalled the most advanced versions of ChatGPT and Claude. passages: Meta has launched what it calls the “most capable” open-weight model in the United States.
Dubbed Muse Spark Open, the model also has the distinction of having been designed to work with Macs.

The new model, which leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, claims to offer superior performance to other popular open-weight models, according to evaluation results released by Meta on Thursday.

Meta says that it paired the model with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, and deployed it to various agentic workflows, including coding fixes for a Mastodon client that included “bug fixes, new features, [and] full build.”

passages: Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight artificial intelligence model that can run locally on Apple’s latest M5 Ultra Mac Studio computers, marking an unusual collaboration between the two technology companies.
The model uses a mixture-of-experts architecture, activating only 42 billion parameters for each token rather than all 816 billion at once.

extraction.body: Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight artificial intelligence model that can run locally on Apple’s latest M5 Ultra Mac Studio computers, marking an unusual collaboration between the two technology companies. The model has been optimised to run across two Apple Mac Studios using Apple’s MLX machine learning framework. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg highlighted the collaboration on X, writing that “Muse Spark Open – weights releasing today – runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple.” Apple CEO John Ternus responded to Zuckerberg, saying it was “amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open’s caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk.” Muse Spark Open has 816 billion total parameters, of which 42 billion are active at a time. It also has a 1-million-token context window and is natively multimodal, meaning it can process text, images, video and audio. Meta says the model has been built for coding and agentic work, including long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering and multi-step reasoning. How Muse Spark Open runs on Apple Mac Studio The Apple connection is significant because a model of this size would normally require data-centre infrastructure. Meta says Muse Spark Open can run on a desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios, with each machine configured with up to 512GB of unified memory. Apple’s MLX framework allows the model to be distributed across the two Macs, with the machines connected using high-speed communication. Apple has also published technical details on running Muse Spark Open across multiple Mac Studios. Meta describes Muse Spark Open as its “most capable US open-weight model to date”. Open-weight models make their trained parameters available to developers, allowing them to download, run and adapt the models rather than accessing them only through a cloud-based service. The model uses a mixture-of-experts architecture, activating only 42 billion parameters for each token rather than all 816 billion at once. This helps make the model more practical to run despite its overall size. Meta says Muse Spark Open has been tested with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, on software engineering tasks, including making bug fixes, adding features and completing a full build of an open-source Mastodon client. The company also tested it with DaVinci Resolve, where the model was able to review footage and identify and crop sections of video. Apple’s testing found that a cluster of four M5 Ultra Mac Studios running Muse Spark Open could generate more than 36 tokens per second. The setup demonstrates how Apple’s unified memory architecture and MLX framework can be used to run large AI models locally. Meta is making Muse Spark Open available through API platforms including Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI. The model weights are also available through platforms including Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden and Microsoft Foundry Models.

extraction.body: Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an open-weight artificial intelligence (AI) model designed for coding, complex reasoning and tasks that require multiple steps. The company says the model can run on a desktop setup using two Apple Mac Studios powered by M5 Ultra chips, making it possible to use an advanced AI model locally rather than relying only on cloud services. As stated by the company in its official announcement, Muse Spark Open has 816 billion total parameters, with 42 billion active parameters, and supports a context window of 1 million tokens. Developers can access the model through several AI platforms or download its weights to customize it for their needs.Meta Muse Spark Open: Features and capabilitiesMeta said Muse Spark Open is designed for long-running tasks, complex software development and agentic AI workflows, in which a model can carry out multiple steps towards a goal.The model is natively multimodal, meaning it can work with different types of information. It has 816 billion total parameters, of which 42 billion are active, and a context window of 1 million tokens. A large context window allows a model to process a substantial amount of information in a single interaction.Meta said it tested the model on tasks involving software development and video editing. In one test, the model was used to make bug fixes and add features to Ice Cubes, an open-source Mastodon client, before building the application. In another, it worked with DaVinci Resolve to review video footage frame by frame, identify suitable moments and crop clips into a vertical format.The company also said the model includes optimised GPU kernels that deliver kernel-level speed improvements of 1.03 to 3.95 times on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. Meta reported a 3% overall speed improvement on AMD MI350.How to access Muse Spark Open AI modelMeta says Muse Spark Open is available through AI inference platforms including Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI. Developers can download its model weights through Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden and Microsoft Foundry Models. The model supports inference engines such as SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, Apple MLX, llama.cpp and Unsloth. Developers can also customise it using PyTorch.For local use, Meta has optimised Muse Spark Open for Apple's M5 Ultra Mac Studio through the MLX framework. According to the company, two Mac Studios can work together to provide enough unified memory to hold the model.Meta said it has added safety training to the open-weight version and evaluated it under its Superintelligence Scaling Framework. The company said the model met the safety thresholds required for release.The model is being released under the Muse Model License, which allows many developers to use it for free but includes limited commercial terms. Its weights are available through the Muse Spark Open collection on Hugging Face.You use AI every day.

passages: Meta has launched what it calls the “most capable” open-weight model in the United States.
Dubbed Muse Spark Open, the model also has the distinction of having been designed to work with Macs.

The new model, which leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, claims to offer superior performance to other popular open-weight models, according to evaluation results released by Meta on Thursday.

Meta says that it paired the model with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, and deployed it to various agentic workflows, including coding fixes for a Mastodon client that included “bug fixes, new features, [and] full build.”

The new model, which leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, claims to offer superior performance to other popular open-weight models, according to evaluation results released by Meta on Thursday. Muse Spark Open is natively multimodal and built for complex coding tasks and agentic labor. It has also been designed to run locally on Apple’s computers. However, you will still need a lot of power to run the model locally, with a requirement of at least 1 terabyte of RAM, per Engadget . The model will run best via the Mac Studio that comes equipped with the M5 Ultra chip. Still, if you can muster the memory, Muse Spark Open may prove a significant work horse for coding and other desktop tasks. Meta says that it paired the model with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, and deployed it to various agentic workflows, including coding fixes for a Mastodon client that included “bug fixes, new features, [and] full build.” The company says it also deployed it in the service of running DaVinci Resolve, the high-end video editing software, revealing that the model was capable of reviewing and cropping footage. Open-weight models provide a number of distinct industry advantages that aren’t afforded by closed and proprietary models. Open-weight models can be significantly more cost-efficient and can also offer transparency and flexibility that closed source models don’t allow. Meta is making the new model available now through a number of different API platforms. The model uses a mixture-of-experts architecture, activating only 42 billion parameters for each token rather than all 816 billion at once.

extraction.body: Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight artificial intelligence model that can run locally on Apple’s latest M5 Ultra Mac Studio computers, marking an unusual collaboration between the two technology companies. The model has been optimised to run across two Apple Mac Studios using Apple’s MLX machine learning framework. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg highlighted the collaboration on X, writing that “Muse Spark Open – weights releasing today – runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple.” Apple CEO John Ternus responded to Zuckerberg, saying it was “amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open’s caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk.” Muse Spark Open has 816 billion total parameters, of which 42 billion are active at a time. It also has a 1-million-token context window and is natively multimodal, meaning it can process text, images, video and audio. Meta says the model has been built for coding and agentic work, including long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering and multi-step reasoning. How Muse Spark Open runs on Apple Mac Studio The Apple connection is significant because a model of this size would normally require data-centre infrastructure. Meta says Muse Spark Open can run on a desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios, with each machine configured with up to 512GB of unified memory. Apple’s MLX framework allows the model to be distributed across the two Macs, with the machines connected using high-speed communication. Apple has also published technical details on running Muse Spark Open across multiple Mac Studios. Meta describes Muse Spark Open as its “most capable US open-weight model to date”. Open-weight models make their trained parameters available to developers, allowing them to download, run and adapt the models rather than accessing them only through a cloud-based service. The model uses a mixture-of-experts architecture, activating only 42 billion parameters for each token rather than all 816 billion at once. This helps make the model more practical to run despite its overall size. Meta says Muse Spark Open has been tested with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, on software engineering tasks, including making bug fixes, adding features and completing a full build of an open-source Mastodon client. The company also tested it with DaVinci Resolve, where the model was able to review footage and identify and crop sections of video. Apple’s testing found that a cluster of four M5 Ultra Mac Studios running Muse Spark Open could generate more than 36 tokens per second. The setup demonstrates how Apple’s unified memory architecture and MLX framework can be used to run large AI models locally. Meta is making Muse Spark Open available through API platforms including Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI. The model weights are also available through platforms including Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden and Microsoft Foundry Models.

extraction.body: Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an open-weight artificial intelligence (AI) model designed for coding, complex reasoning and tasks that require multiple steps. The company says the model can run on a desktop setup using two Apple Mac Studios powered by M5 Ultra chips, making it possible to use an advanced AI model locally rather than relying only on cloud services. As stated by the company in its official announcement, Muse Spark Open has 816 billion total parameters, with 42 billion active parameters, and supports a context window of 1 million tokens. Developers can access the model through several AI platforms or download its weights to customize it for their needs.Meta Muse Spark Open: Features and capabilitiesMeta said Muse Spark Open is designed for long-running tasks, complex software development and agentic AI workflows, in which a model can carry out multiple steps towards a goal.The model is natively multimodal, meaning it can work with different types of information. It has 816 billion total parameters, of which 42 billion are active, and a context window of 1 million tokens. A large context window allows a model to process a substantial amount of information in a single interaction.Meta said it tested the model on tasks involving software development and video editing. In one test, the model was used to make bug fixes and add features to Ice Cubes, an open-source Mastodon client, before building the application. In another, it worked with DaVinci Resolve to review video footage frame by frame, identify suitable moments and crop clips into a vertical format.The company also said the model includes optimised GPU kernels that deliver kernel-level speed improvements of 1.03 to 3.95 times on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. Meta reported a 3% overall speed improvement on AMD MI350.How to access Muse Spark Open AI modelMeta says Muse Spark Open is available through AI inference platforms including Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI. Developers can download its model weights through Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden and Microsoft Foundry Models. The model supports inference engines such as SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, Apple MLX, llama.cpp and Unsloth. Developers can also customise it using PyTorch.For local use, Meta has optimised Muse Spark Open for Apple's M5 Ultra Mac Studio through the MLX framework. According to the company, two Mac Studios can work together to provide enough unified memory to hold the model.Meta said it has added safety training to the open-weight version and evaluated it under its Superintelligence Scaling Framework. The company said the model met the safety thresholds required for release.The model is being released under the Muse Model License, which allows many developers to use it for free but includes limited commercial terms. Its weights are available through the Muse Spark Open collection on Hugging Face.You use AI every day.

extraction.body: Tim Cook and Mark Zuckerberg have clashed for years, but with John Ternus taking the reins at Apple , the rivals are finding common ground in artificial intelligence. Meta and Apple revealed a new collaboration Thursday that will enable developers to easily run Meta's new open-weight AI model on Apple's high-end desktop computers. The collaboration centers on Muse Spark Open, the most capable open-weight model released under a license that allows for limited commercial use, according to Meta. It's an 816-billion-parameter model using a so-called mixture-of-experts architecture . As an open-weight model, developers can download the technology's parameters, or weights, from the internet and run the model on a wide range of hardware. Customers will be able to pair between two and four Mac Studio PCs to use Muse Spark to code, analyze video or do other agentic work. The model runs locally, instead of in the cloud, adding a layer of security and saving users money, the companies said. Thursday's announcement, following months of collaboration, is a sign that the AI boom has shifted historical alliances in Silicon Valley. For years, Apple and Meta regarded each other warily and avoided public partnerships, and the relationship hit rock bottom after Apple introduced privacy changes in 2021 that limited the targeting capabilities of digital ad companies. Meta estimated in early 2022 that the change would cut its revenue that year by $10 billion. Representatives from Apple and Meta declined to say if the Muse Spark Open collaboration was the start of a deeper relationship. Zuckerberg posted a picture on X showing the Meta agent working on a Mac computer. He wrote, "Muse Spark Open -- weights releasing today -- runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple." Ternus responded , "Congrats to the team! Amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open's caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk. Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI!" Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said in an interview that many powerful open-weight models are too big to be run on the majority of personal computers, but Apple's Mac Studios make enough memory available to users so that it's practical to run Muse Spark Open. The move represents an important show of confidence in Meta's rebooted AI efforts and could pose a challenge to OpenAI and Anthropic. It could also signal Apple's growing strength in AI chips, a market that Nvidia has dominated so far due to their prevalence in large data centers. " We worked with Apple to bring leading Agent capabilities to your desktop for the first time on the Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios, so you know we're really excited about this," Wang said. Developers can download a version of the AI model from websites like Hugging Face without extra configuration for Apple's silicon. Muse Spark Open has also been tuned to run faster on Apple's hardware, and the iPhone maker revealed new benchmarks for its chips and published technical documentation about its MLX AI framework's ability to split open-source models across multiple machines. Mac Studios aren't cheap though, and this AI model requires the fastest Apple chips and as much memory as possible. Currently, a Mac Studio with the required M5 Ultra chip and 256GB of memory costs at least $10,799. A more expensive version with 512GB of RAM will be released later this month. Plus, users will need to buy multiple machines. The two companies are collaborating on open-source AI, which has become a point of contention in Washington as politicians worry that free Chinese models could undercut American AI. Although Meta once centered its AI strategy on its older open-weight Llama family of models , it has since focused on creating proprietary models under the leadership of Wang , who joined Meta when the company invested more than $14 billion into his former startup Scale AI last year. While Apple and Meta, then known as Facebook, partnered on iPhone extensions over a decade ago, they haven't struck any public partnerships since 2017 after Apple removed system-level Facebook integration from the iPhone. "Most of the animosity predates my tenure at the company, but obviously there's been a long history between Meta and Apple," Wang said, pointing to one member of his team, AI researcher and former Apple director Daniel Gross, as a reason for the collaboration. Gross, along with former GitHub CEO Nat Friedman , was a major Zuckerberg hire last year as the Facebook founder was overhauling his company's AI strategy. Cook, who was Apple CEO until Ternus succeeded him last month, took a shot at Zuckerberg in 2018, during the Cambridge Analytica scandal, saying, "I wouldn't be in this situation." Cook often criticized Meta for compromising user privacy. Zuckerberg has also insulted Apple in public, telling Joe Rogan last year that the company "hasn't invented anything great since the iPhone." Meta and Apple revealed a new collaboration Thursday that will enable developers to easily run Meta's new open-weight AI model on Apple's high-end desktop computers.

The collaboration centers on Muse Spark Open, the most capable open-weight model released under a license that allows for limited commercial use, according to Meta. It's an 816-billion-parameter model using a so-called mixture-of-experts architecture . As an open-weight model, developers can download the technology's parameters, or weights, from the internet and run the model on a wide range of hardware.

Customers will be able to pair between two and four Mac Studio PCs to use Muse Spark to code, analyze video or do other agentic work. The model runs locally, instead of in the cloud, adding a layer of security and saving users money, the companies said.

Thursday's announcement, following months of collaboration, is a sign that the AI boom has shifted historical alliances in Silicon Valley. For years, Apple and Meta regarded each other warily and avoided public partnerships, and the relationship hit rock bottom after Apple introduced privacy changes in 2021 that limited the targeting capabilities of digital ad companies. Meta estimated in early 2022 that the change would cut its revenue that year by $10 billion.

sources.title: Apple and Meta Team Up to Run Muse Spark Open Locally on Four Mac Studios
passages: Apple and Meta have worked together to run Metas new Muse Spark Open AI model entirely on Mac Studio hardware, with no cloud servers involved.
Apple says you need either two M5 Ultra Mac Studios with 512GB of unified memory each, or four with 256GB each.
In Apples own tests, four Mac Studios generated more than 36 tokens per second.

The four-machine setup works today, while the 512GB configuration ships only in late October.Apples open-source MLX framework splits the model across the connected Macs, which talk to each other over Thunderbolt 5.

extraction.body: Apple and Meta have worked together to run Metas new Muse Spark Open AI model entirely on Mac Studio hardware, with no cloud servers involved. It is an unusual partnership, given how often the two companies have clashed over privacy and advertising. Here, though, both have something to gain.Muse Spark Open is an open-weight model that Meta announced on October 15. The model is huge, as it has 816 billion parameters, with 42 billion active at any time, and its compressed weights alone take up about 493GB.You will need more than one Mac StudioA single Mac cannot hold a model this big. Apple says you need either two M5 Ultra Mac Studios with 512GB of unified memory each, or four with 256GB each. The four-machine setup works today, while the 512GB configuration ships only in late October.Apples open-source MLX framework splits the model across the connected Macs, which talk to each other over Thunderbolt 5. In Apples own tests, four Mac Studios generated more than 36 tokens per second. In demos, the model fixed bugs in an open-source iOS app and cut vertical clips from footage in DaVinci Resolve, all on local hardware.The catch is the price. The M5 Ultra Mac Studio starts at Rs 6,29,900 in India, so four base units alone cost over Rs 25 lakh before any memory upgrades. This is clearly meant for developers, research labs and companies that do not want sensitive code leaving the office.What is the Windows equivalent?On the PC side, the closest match is Nvidias DGX Station for Windows, which Nvidia built with Microsoft and announced at Computex 2026. It runs on the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra chip with up to 748GB of memory, enough to fit a model like Muse Spark Open in a single box instead of four. Meta says Muse Spark Open also supports Nvidia, AMD and Intel hardware, but it has not shown the model running on a Windows workstation yet.For regular PC buyers, a model this size is out of reach on any platform. Laptops and mini PCs with AMDs Ryzen AI Max chips and 128GB of memory can run smaller open models. That includes Metas own 30-billion-parameter Muse Glimmer, which was released in August and runs on a single GPU.Muse Spark Open is available on Hugging Face, and developers without the hardware can use it through hosted API providers.

extraction.body: Tim Cook and Mark Zuckerberg have clashed for years, but with John Ternus taking the reins at Apple , the rivals are finding common ground in artificial intelligence. Meta and Apple revealed a new collaboration Thursday that will enable developers to easily run Meta's new open-weight AI model on Apple's high-end desktop computers. The collaboration centers on Muse Spark Open, the most capable open-weight model released under a license that allows for limited commercial use, according to Meta. It's an 816-billion-parameter model using a so-called mixture-of-experts architecture . As an open-weight model, developers can download the technology's parameters, or weights, from the internet and run the model on a wide range of hardware. Customers will be able to pair between two and four Mac Studio PCs to use Muse Spark to code, analyze video or do other agentic work. The model runs locally, instead of in the cloud, adding a layer of security and saving users money, the companies said. Thursday's announcement, following months of collaboration, is a sign that the AI boom has shifted historical alliances in Silicon Valley. For years, Apple and Meta regarded each other warily and avoided public partnerships, and the relationship hit rock bottom after Apple introduced privacy changes in 2021 that limited the targeting capabilities of digital ad companies. Meta estimated in early 2022 that the change would cut its revenue that year by $10 billion. Representatives from Apple and Meta declined to say if the Muse Spark Open collaboration was the start of a deeper relationship. Zuckerberg posted a picture on X showing the Meta agent working on a Mac computer. He wrote, "Muse Spark Open -- weights releasing today -- runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple." Ternus responded , "Congrats to the team! Amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open's caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk. Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI!" Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said in an interview that many powerful open-weight models are too big to be run on the majority of personal computers, but Apple's Mac Studios make enough memory available to users so that it's practical to run Muse Spark Open. The move represents an important show of confidence in Meta's rebooted AI efforts and could pose a challenge to OpenAI and Anthropic. sources.title: Apple and Meta Team Up to Run Muse Spark Open Locally on Four Mac Studios
passages: Apple and Meta have worked together to run Metas new Muse Spark Open AI model entirely on Mac Studio hardware, with no cloud servers involved.
Apple says you need either two M5 Ultra Mac Studios with 512GB of unified memory each, or four with 256GB each.
In Apples own tests, four Mac Studios generated more than 36 tokens per second.

The four-machine setup works today, while the 512GB configuration ships only in late October.Apples open-source MLX framework splits the model across the connected Macs, which talk to each other over Thunderbolt 5.
